title: Matchmaker
novel:
Ted booked an [[appointment|appointment]] at a small [[matchmaking|matchmaking]] [[agency|agency]] on the fourteenth floor.

The [[matchmaker|matchmaker]] gave him a [[questionnaire|questionnaire]] with ninety questions. She said her [[algorithm|algorithm]] had never failed. She showed him [[charts|chart]], [[statistics|statistics]], and a huge [[database|database]] of lonely [[clients|clients]].

"We [[guarantee|guarantee]] your [[soulmate|soulmate]]," she said.

Ted was [[sceptical|sceptical]] but hopeful. He listed his [[criteria|criteria]] carefully. The machine thought for a while and found exactly one [[compatible|compatible]] woman in the whole city.

One. The [[odds|odds]] were terrible.

The [[blind date|blind date]] was arranged. Ted arrived early, wearing his best shirt, feeling almost [[flawless|flawless]].

Then the woman appeared — wearing a ring. She had got engaged two days before. Ted laughed to hide his [[panic|panic]].

So the search had been [[in vain|in vain]]. The agency [[rejected|reject]] his request for a second name, because there was no second name.

Walking home he thought about it. Perhaps he was too [[picky|picky]]; perhaps everyone else had learned to [[settle for|settle for]] something smaller.

But he did not want a match calculated by a computer. He wanted the [[accidental|accidental]] kind — the kind you cannot put in a form.

appointment.en: a time you have arranged to meet someone

matchmaking.en: the job of finding a partner for someone

agency.en: a company that does a service for other people

matchmaker.en: a person who tries to bring two single people together

questionnaire.en: a list of questions you answer on paper

algorithm.en: a set of steps a computer follows to solve a problem

chart.en: a drawing that shows numbers or information

statistics.en: numbers that show facts about a group of things

database.en: a large store of information kept on a computer

clients.en: people who pay for a service

guarantee.en: to promise firmly that something will happen

soulmate.en: the one person who understands you perfectly

sceptical.en: not ready to believe that something is true

criteria.en: the rules you use to judge or choose something

compatible.en: able to live or work well together

odds.en: how likely it is that something will happen

blind date.en: a meeting with someone you have never seen before, to see if you like each other

panic.en: a sudden strong feeling of fear

reject.en: to say no to something or someone

picky.en: very hard to please; choosing too carefully

settle for.en: to accept something that is not as good as you wanted

accidental.en: happening by chance, not by plan
